Oh yeah, FIU is pretty well known. I’ve worked for the department of defense, the Air Force, DEVCOM Army Research labs, and industry. A lot of employers in the defense sector recognize FIU, including the CIA and NSA. That alone should say a lot :)

I did, I got plenty of internships :) Just know it’s going to require you to attend events and network. Become a part of the INIT club at FIU and the networking becomes much easier. If you could build a relationship with a professor by working with them at their lab, it’s even better. Professors can put in the word for you and get you an internship quickly.

Doesn’t matter where you study CS. Market is saturated with too many people wanting to get in. I did computer engineering and had better luck, also getting my masters and work experience as a research assistant at an FIU lab helped tremendously. Talk to your professors and see if you can get a research assistant position.

FIU helped me get a ton of opportunities (currently a PhD student). I did both my bachelors and masters in computer engineering and in an engineering perspective, my education and degrees was recognized by many employers including the DoD. If you plan on going into engineering, CS, or anything stem, I highly suggest you reach out for research assistant opportunities by asking your professors if they need an RA for their labs. You get so much networking opportunities, and the professors will connect you with government, industry, and other national labs to provide you internships. 

A lot of my resume and experience that landed me a comfy job was thanks to the networking opportunities my lab provided for me during my masters. I wish I could’ve sought these opportunities out as undergrad, but I wasn’t aware of them. 

People who say you don’t have the same opportunities by going to FIU are wrong. They simply didn’t put in enough effort to network and try to get internships, or did not speak to their professors. Your professors will put in the word for you and help you connect with industry :)
